properties.description: Rake (2011) is an Australian comedy-drama starring Richard Roxburgh, with supporting performances from Matt Day and Kate Box; writers on the series include Peter Duncan, Andrew Knight and Charles Waterstreet. It follows a brilliant but self-destructive criminal lawyer who repeatedly wins improbable cases while his personal life — marked by addiction, gambling debt and fraught relationships — spirals. Tonally the series mixes dark satire, courtroom drama and seedy, character-driven comedy to probe questions of justice, corruption and personal morality. The result is often uproarious, frequently uncomfortable, and anchored by a charismatic antihero performance.
properties.plot_summary: A brilliant but self-destructive criminal lawyer repeatedly wins apparently unwinnable cases while his private life unravels: addiction, massive gambling debt and chaotic relationships. He navigates Sydney’s courts and seedy underworld with sharp wit and moral flexibility, often creating as many problems as he solves. Episodes blend courtroom battles with dark, satirical set pieces that expose corruption, politics and personal compromise.

properties.description: The Split (2018), directed in part by Jessica Hobbs, is a British legal-family drama led by Nicola Walker as the central divorce lawyer, with Stephen Mangan among the principal cast. Set in London’s family-law scene, the series follows a woman torn between a prestigious firm and the rival practice run by her own family as she handles high-stakes divorces, custody disputes, and ethically fraught client work. Grounded in intimate character study, the show explores themes of familial loyalty, professional rivalry, love and betrayal, and personal growth through a palette of realistic legal procedure and emotionally resonant family storytelling. Its tone is serious and nuanced, combining courtroom tension with domestic drama and placing moral ambiguity and relational complexity at the heart of its narrative.
properties.plot_summary: A family of high-powered divorce lawyers navigate the emotional and procedural complexities of marital breakdowns while their own relationships fray under pressure. The central figure is a driven divorce lawyer who splits her time between a prominent London practice and the private turmoil of her family’s rival firm. Cases range from delicate negotiations and custody battles to acrimonious courtroom showdowns, each illuminating the personal histories, secrets, and loyalties that bind and break the family. Professional rivalries, ethical dilemmas, and overlapping client conflicts force the characters to confront compromises between career ambition and private life, and to reckon with past choices that shape both their marriages and their legal strategies.

properties.description: Here and Now (2018), created by Alan Ball and starring Tim Robbins, Holly Hunter, and Daniel Zovatto, is a dark comedy-drama that follows a progressive Portland family as personal crises expose cultural and psychological fault lines. The series alternates between dry humor and unsettling, sometimes fantastical episodes that test empathy and belief. properties.description: Sisters (released 2018) is a comedy-drama starring Lucy Durack, Antonia Prebble and Maria Angelico that follows three women who discover they are biological sisters after uncovering that their father used his own sperm in IVF procedures. properties.plot_summary: Three women from different walks of life discover they are biological sisters after one of them learns their Nobel-Prize-winning father secretly used his own sperm in multiple IVF procedures. The series follows Julia, an amiable but aimless woman who uncovers the truth, Roxy, a children's TV presenter struggling with pills, and Edie, an uptight lawyer dealing with personal upheaval. It balances darkly comic moments with heartfelt, character-driven drama as the trio navigate surprising connections and emotional fallout.

properties.description: The Durrells (2016) is a British comedy-drama, directed in part by Steve Barron and Roger Goldby, that adapts the autobiographical writings of a naturalist to the screen. Starring Keeley Hawes as the widowed matriarch alongside Josh O’Connor, Callum Woodhouse, Daisy Waterstone and Milo Parker as her four children, the series follows their relocation from Bournemouth to a Greek island in the 1930s. Combining period-family drama and gentle comedy, the show traces the family’s financial struggles, cultural adjustments, romantic entanglements, and the youngest child’s growing obsession with wildlife. Thematically it centers on family resilience, adaptation, and a deep appreciation for nature, while tonally remaining warm, nostalgic and whimsical—offering viewers soothing, character-driven episodes set against idyllic island scenery.
properties.plot_summary: A recently widowed mother uproots her four children from a modest English seaside town to a sun-drenched Ionian island in the mid-1930s seeking a cheaper, healthier life. The family must learn to navigate a slower, more communal island existence while wrestling with money worries, matrimonial prospects, artistic ambitions, and clashing personalities. The eldest son pursues literary dreams and complicated relationships; the teenage daughter tests boundaries and searches for independence; the awkward, outdoorsy son finds freedom in the countryside; and the youngest becomes obsessively fascinated with local flora and fauna, collecting animals and studying nature. Each episode follows their small-scale adventures and misadventures—romantic entanglements, local customs, entrepreneurial schemes, and conservation-minded escapades—blending gentle comedy with tender family moments as they settle into a new culture and landscape.
properties.genre_description: A character-driven comedy-drama set within a historical period context. It mixes elements of family drama and slice-of-life storytelling with biographical inspiration, emphasizing episodic, interpersonal plots over serialized high-stakes conflict. Visual and narrative cues place it firmly in period-piece and pastoral subgenres, with a focus on interpersonal relationships and everyday adventures.
properties.style_description: Sun-drenched, picturesque cinematography with warm color palettes and attention to landscape and rural detail. properties.description: Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha (2021), directed by Yoo Je-won, is a South Korean romantic comedy-drama starring Shin Min-a and Kim Seon-ho (with Lee Sang-yi in a key supporting role). Loosely adapted from the 2004 film Mr. Handy, Mr. Hong, the series follows a pragmatic dentist who leaves Seoul and a beloved local jack-of-all-trades whose quiet competence anchors a seaside village. Across its episodes the show blends warm romantic development with episodic, slice-of-life stories about the village’s residents, exploring themes of love, community, personal growth, and recovery from past hurts. Tonally it is heartwarming and uplifting, relying on gentle humor, tender emotional beats, and scenic coastal visuals to create a comforting, restorative viewing experience.
properties.plot_summary: A pragmatic, perfectionist dentist from Seoul relocates to a tranquil seaside village after a sudden life change. In the close-knit community she encounters a resourceful, good-natured jack-of-all-trades known for quietly solving residents’ problems and for being deeply integrated into village life. As they interact, professional friction and contrasting worldviews give way to mutual respect, attraction, and emotional support. Parallel storylines follow quirky townspeople—shopkeepers, elders, friends—whose small conflicts and everyday needs reveal long-held wounds, personal growth, and the ways community ties foster healing. Over the course of the series, both leads confront past hurts, learn to rely on others, and find belonging and new beginnings in the rhythms of small-town life.

properties.description: Welcome to Samdalri (2023), directed by Cha Young-hoon, is a romantic comedy–leaning comedy-drama centered on two childhood friends who reunite on a scenic island after years apart. Focusing on the characters Cho Yong-pil and Cho Sam-dal (who lives for a time as Cho Eun-hye), the series blends lighthearted romantic moments with reflective, slice-of-life scenes as it explores themes of friendship, grief, reconciliation, and the tug between dreams and home. Tonally warm and nostalgic with touches of whimsy, the show uses vibrant, cinematic visuals of coastal life and quiet, character-focused storytelling to deliver an emotionally resonant, heartwarming viewing experience.
properties.plot_summary: Two childhood friends from a small coastal town follow divergent paths only to be drawn back together by circumstance and memory. One, hardened by the early loss of his mother, trains himself as a weather forecaster to shield his community from rumors and falsehoods; the other reinvents herself in the city as a fashion photographer under a new name, chasing ambition and distance from her past. When setbacks in her metropolitan life force her return to their seaside hometown, their old bond is reopened and they must confront unresolved pain, changing dreams, and the ways they hurt and protect each other. The story traces their slow, sometimes awkward reconnection as they rebuild trust, reevaluate what success and home mean, and gradually allow love and forgiveness to reshape their futures.
